headline: Rocket Launch and Wildlife Viewing Reservations
reservation: Access to Cocoa Beach is generally open, but Kennedy Space Center tours and launch viewing sites require separate paid tickets. Seasonal bioluminescence tours and glamping sites in the Merritt Island area often book months in advance; always verify current procedures on the official Space Coast or National Wildlife Refuge sites.

days.title: Surf History and Coastal Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Downtown Cocoa Beach

stops.name: Florida Surf Museum
stops.detail: Explore the evolution of East Coast surfing and local legends like Kelly Slater through vintage boards and cultural exhibits.

stops.name: Cocoa Beach Pier
stops.detail: Walk this 800-foot historic wooden landmark to view surfers from above and browse local seaside boutiques.

days.driving: Allow 15–20 minutes for local beach traffic; conditions vary.
days.note: Parking near the pier is limited during spring break and holiday weekends.

days.title: Lagoon Ecology and Wildlife

stops.name: Thousand Islands
stops.detail: Navigate a labyrinth of mangrove tunnels by kayak to spot West Indian manatees and bottlenose dolphins.

stops.name: Lori Wilson Park
stops.detail: Walk the maritime hammock boardwalk trail to see a more natural side of the Florida dunes.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes between lagoon launches and coastal parks.
days.note: Summer lagoon outings should be planned early to avoid mid-day humidity.

days.title: Space Age Exploration

stops.name: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex
stops.detail: Visit the Rocket Garden and see the Space Shuttle Atlantis at this world-class science facility.

stops.name: Merritt Island National Wildlife Refuge
stops.detail: Drive the Black Point Wildlife Drive to view roseate spoonbills and migratory birds in their natural habitat.

days.driving: Allow 45–60 minutes; traffic increases significantly on rocket launch days.
days.note: Refuge access may be restricted during active launch windows for safety.

intel.title: Public Beach Access
intel.text: Paid parking lots are common near the Pier and Minutemen Causeway; check local signage for hourly rates. Arrive early at Lori Wilson Park for free parking options which often reach capacity by noon.

intel.title: Lagoon Connectivity
intel.text: Cell service is reliable in town but may drop while deep inside the Thousand Islands mangrove canopy. Download offline navigation if you are paddling without a professional local guide.

intel.title: Refuge Logistics
intel.text: Fuel up in Titusville or Cocoa Beach before entering Merritt Island National Wildlife Refuge. There are no gas stations or commercial services within the interior sections of the refuge.

intel.title: Seasonal Bioluminescence
intel.text: Summer months offer the best viewing for glowing dinoflagellates in the Banana River. These night tours are highly weather-dependent and require advanced booking through authorized outfitters.

intel.title: Beach Ramp Rules
intel.text: Check the City of Cocoa Beach website for current dog-friendly beach zones and designated times. Driving on the sand is prohibited in this region; use established beach ramps for foot access only.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at MLB airport, then head north for 45 minutes to Cocoa Beach for a supply run at the A1A grocery hubs before check-in.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for paved coastal roads; check rental agreements for restrictions on unpaved refuge roads.
plan.goldenHour: Cocoa Beach Pier for views of the Atlantic surf, with the caveat that sunrise provides better light for water photography.
